HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:14:02 GMT
Server: webs
Content-Length: 237
Connection: keep-alive
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
Cache-Control: no-store
Pragma: no-cache
Content-Type: application/xml

<ResponseStatus><statusCode>4</statusCode><statusString>Invalid Operation</statusString><subStatusCode>authFailed</subStatusCode><lockStatus>unlock</lockStatus><unlockTime>0</unlockTime><retryLoginTime>4</retryLoginTime></ResponseStatus>

INVENTED-BUT-LABELLED — NOT A DEVICE CAPTURE. (card t_a3521d8a)
Shape (c), and the one that reproduces the live failure: a 401 that carries an ISAPI
error envelope and **no `WWW-Authenticate` header at all**. Note what is absent — no
challenge means httpx.DigestAuth returns the response untouched (its re-pay is gated
on the header, `_auth.py:201`), so the client keeps presenting the retired nonce and
the walk dies: exit 3 at the request where the nonce aged out, with the CORRECT
password and the device unlocked — exactly docs/OBSERVED.md "Digest nonce use-cap".
`lockStatus=unlock` / `unlockTime=0` mirror the owner's post-mortem read of the device
(unlocked, retryLoginTime=4), which is why recovery is allowed here and never when the
body says `locked`. Style follows the recorded `error_naive_start_time.json` /
`digest_challenge_401.txt` envelopes; `authFailed` as a subStatusCode is invented.
Served by: FakeDevice(retire_shape=RETIRE_ENVELOPE_ONLY).
Client outcome (probe, docs/FINDINGS-t_a3521d8a.md F1): the pre-fix client died here at
request N+1 and opened the circuit; the fix drops the digest state (nonce AND nc) and
re-issues the identical request, which re-bootstraps via a normal challenge.
